key_insight: Sb doping in Na/K-alloyed Cs2BInCl6 double perovskite nanocrystals creates self-trapped excitons that strongly red-shift photoluminescence, while B-site composition selectively tunes the exciton lattice distortion and polarization anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: This work identifies composition knobs for tuning color output and exciton behavior in lead-free perovskites, useful for designing stable optoelectronic and photocatalytic materials.
method: Optical spectroscopy of Sb-doped Cs2BInCl6 nanocrystals across Na-to-K B-site alloying
Ab initio calculations of excitonic states, radiative channels, and lattice distortions
Time-resolved polarization-anisotropy measurements to test predicted wavefunction fingerprints
evidence_signal: PL shifts from about 2.48 to 2.70 eV while the absorption feature near 3.8 eV remains nearly unchanged, and measured anisotropy closely matches theory.
watch_item: The conclusions rely on nanocrystal composition control and model-dependent interpretation of exciton-phonon coupling, so broader material generalization may require additional validation.
paper_title: Composition-controlled optical fingerprints and anisotropy of self-trapped excitons in double perovskites
